MEDIUM — We are modifying a database constraint. Done correctly, this is safe. The SQL below drops the old constraint and adds the correct one. No data is deleted. Existing rep and manager roles are unaffected.

What Could Break

-- Step 1: Drop the old constraint that only allows rep and manager
ALTER TABLE reps DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS reps_role_check;

Exact SQL to Run

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION set_activity_code()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  submitted_date   date;
  activity_dow     int;
  next_working_day date;
BEGIN
  -- Auto-generate activity code
  IF new.activity_code IS NULL THEN
    new.activity_code := 'ACT-' || lpad(nextval('activity_code_seq')::text, 5, '0');
  END IF;

  -- Set month label
  IF new.activity_date IS NOT NULL THEN
    new.month := to_char(new.activity_date, 'Month YYYY');
  END IF;

  -- Set submission status
  IF new.submission_status IS NULL THEN
    submitted_date := date(new.submitted_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Riyadh');
    activity_dow   := EXTRACT(DOW FROM new.activity_date); -- 0=Sun, 5=Fri, 6=Sat

    -- Weekend activities: always on_time, no submission expected
    IF activity_dow IN (5, 6) THEN
      new.submission_status := 'on_time';

    -- Same day submission: on_time
    ELSIF submitted_date = new.activity_date THEN
      new.submission_status := 'on_time';

    -- Submitted after activity date: check against next working day
    ELSIF submitted_date > new.activity_date THEN
      next_working_day := new.activity_date + 1;

      -- Skip Friday (5) and Saturday (6)
      WHILE EXTRACT(DOW FROM next_working_day) IN (5, 6) LOOP
        next_working_day := next_working_day + 1;
      END LOOP;

      IF submitted_date <= next_working_day THEN
        new.submission_status := 'on_time';
      ELSE
        new.submission_status := 'late';
      END IF;

    END IF;
  END IF;

  RETURN new;
END;
$$;

Step 2 — Create the Database Function

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION detect_duplicate_companies()
RETURNS integer LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER AS $$
DECLARE
  new_flags integer := 0;
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO duplicate_flags (
    company_id_1, company_id_2, match_type, match_key, classification
  )
  SELECT
    a.id,
    b.id,
    'name',
    a.company_name,
    'pending'
  FROM companies a
  JOIN companies b ON b.id > a.id
  WHERE
    a.status = 'active'
    AND b.status = 'active'
    AND (
      -- Exact normalized match
      a.company_name_normalized = b.company_name_normalized
      OR
      -- High similarity match using pg_trgm (threshold 0.6)
      similarity(
        COALESCE(a.company_name_normalized, a.company_name),
        COALESCE(b.company_name_normalized, b.company_name)
      ) > 0.6
    )
    -- Skip pairs already flagged
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM duplicate_flags df
      WHERE (df.company_id_1 = a.id AND df.company_id_2 = b.id)
      OR    (df.company_id_1 = b.id AND df.company_id_2 = a.id)
    );

  GET DIAGNOSTICS new_flags = ROW_COUNT;
  RETURN new_flags;
END;
$$;

Phase 4.5b — Fix Holiday Excuse Not Working in Notifications

Goal

When a company holiday is added, the dashboard correctly shows reps as "Excused". But the check_missing_submissions function that fires notifications has a logic flaw — it skips the holiday day entirely and goes back to the previous working day, then checks if reps submitted for THAT day. So reps still get "missing" notifications for the day before the holiday.

Root Cause

The current function does this:

Start from yesterday

If yesterday was a holiday → go back one more day

Check submissions for THAT earlier day

This is wrong. It should do this:

Start from yesterday

If yesterday was a holiday or weekend → reps are excused, fire NO notifications at all

If yesterday was a normal working day → check submissions for yesterday only

Risk Level

MEDIUM — Replacing a database function. Rollback SQL provided.

Exact SQL to Run

Go to Supabase → SQL Editor → paste this → Run:

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION check_missing_submissions()
RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER AS $$
DECLARE
  yesterday        date;
  yesterday_dow    int;
  rep_record       RECORD;
  manager_record   RECORD;
  already_notified boolean;
  is_excused       boolean;
BEGIN
  yesterday     := CURRENT_DATE - 1;
  yesterday_dow := EXTRACT(DOW FROM yesterday);

  -- Step 1: If yesterday was a weekend, do nothing at all
  IF yesterday_dow IN (5, 6) THEN
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  -- Step 2: If yesterday was a company holiday, do nothing at all
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM company_holidays
    WHERE yesterday BETWEEN date_from AND date_to
  ) THEN
    RETURN;
  END IF;

  -- Step 3: Yesterday was a real working day — check each rep
  FOR rep_record IN
    SELECT id, name
    FROM reps
    WHERE status = 'active'
    AND role IN ('rep', 'marketing')
  LOOP
    -- Check if this rep has an approved absence for yesterday
    SELECT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM rep_absences
      WHERE rep_id = rep_record.id
      AND yesterday BETWEEN date_from AND date_to
    ) INTO is_excused;

    -- Skip excused reps silently
    IF is_excused THEN
      CONTINUE;
    END IF;

    -- Check if rep submitted anything for yesterday
    IF NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM activities
      WHERE rep_id = rep_record.id
      AND activity_date = yesterday
    ) THEN
      -- Only notify if we haven't already notified today
      SELECT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM notifications
        WHERE recipient_id = rep_record.id
        AND type = 'missing_submission'
        AND created_at::date = CURRENT_DATE
        AND body LIKE '%' || yesterday::text || '%'
      ) INTO already_notified;

      IF NOT already_notified THEN
        -- Notify the rep
        INSERT INTO notifications (
          recipient_id, type, title, body, entity_type
        ) VALUES (
          rep_record.id,
          'missing_submission',
          'Missing Daily Report',
          'You have not submitted your daily report for ' ||
            to_char(yesterday, 'DD Mon YYYY') ||
            '. Please submit it or ask your manager to record an absence.',
          'rep'
        );

        -- Notify all managers
        FOR manager_record IN
          SELECT id FROM reps
          WHERE status = 'active'
          AND role IN ('manager', 'super_admin')
        LOOP
          SELECT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM notifications
            WHERE recipient_id = manager_record.id
            AND type = 'missing_submission'
            AND created_at::date = CURRENT_DATE
            AND body LIKE '%' || rep_record.name || '%'
            AND body LIKE '%' || yesterday::text || '%'
          ) INTO already_notified;

          IF NOT already_notified THEN
            INSERT INTO notifications (
              recipient_id, type, title, body, entity_type
            ) VALUES (
              manager_record.id,
              'missing_submission',
              'Missing Report: ' || rep_record.name,
              rep_record.name || ' has not submitted their daily report for ' ||
                to_char(yesterday, 'DD Mon YYYY') || '.',
              'rep'
            );
          END IF;
        END LOOP;

      END IF;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END;
$$;

What This Does

Right now projects.quoted_sqm is set manually when creating a project. Once a coordinator enters quotations, those numbers should drive the project totals automatically. This phase adds a DB trigger so that:

projects.quoted_sqm = sum of all quotation sqm_quoted for that project

No UI changes. DB only.

Step 1 — Create the trigger function

Run in Supabase SQL Editor:

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_project_sqm()
RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $$
DECLARE
  v_project_id uuid;
BEGIN
  -- Works for INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
  v_project_id := COALESCE(NEW.project_id, OLD.project_id);
  IF v_project_id IS NULL THEN RETURN NEW; END IF;

  UPDATE projects
  SET
    quoted_sqm = (
      SELECT COALESCE(SUM(sqm_quoted), 0)
      FROM quotations
      WHERE project_id = v_project_id
        AND status NOT IN ('cancelled')
    ),
    won_sqm = (
      SELECT COALESCE(SUM(sqm_invoiced), 0)
      FROM quotations
      WHERE project_id = v_project_id
        AND status = 'won'
    ),
    updated_at = now()
  WHERE id = v_project_id;

  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

Step 2 — Attach the trigger to quotations

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_sync_project_sqm ON quotations;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_sync_project_sqm
  AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OR DELETE ON quotations
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_project_sqm();

## Supabase Nested Select Fix
Supabase returns joined tables as arrays. TypeScript expects objects.

type Project = { companies: any; project_reps: { role: string; reps: any }[] };

Fix: remove the join, look up from already-loaded reps array client-side:
